name: Autonomy

subjectOf.text: Even if every user and supporter of the blockchain and their locations were known, it would still not be possible to exercise jurisdiction in the traditional meaning of the word, because the system operates largely autonomously.
subjectOf.abstract: Because the system operates largely autonomously, even if every user and supporter of the blockchain and their location were known, it would still not be possible to exercise jurisdiction in the traditional meaning of the word.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Craig Calcaterra, Crypto Transaction Dispute Resolution (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2992962

subjectOf.text: The platform's feedback loop is closed in the sense that there are no rent seeking owners: the system is entirely supported by its users and the users reap the entire profit.
subjectOf.abstract: Therefore the feedback loop of the platform is closed, in the sense that there are no rent-seeking6 owners: The system is entirely supported by users, and the users reap the entire profit.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vlad Andrei, Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125822
scope_conditions: all fees are disbursed to expert users
no outside owner holds a claim on fees

subjectOf.text: The platform becomes fully autonomous almost immediately after deployment, because once the Ethereum DApp is posted its authors have no more control over the evolution of the expertise tags than any other Ethereum user.
subjectOf.abstract: The platform achieves full autonomy almost immediately. Once the Ethereum DApp is posted to the blockchain, its authors have no more control over the evolution of the expertise tags in its forum than any other Ethereum user.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vlad Andrei, Blockchain Infrastructure for Measuring Domain Specific Reputation in Autonomous Decentralized and A (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3125822
scope_conditions: after the DApp is deployed to the blockchain

subjectOf.text: Centralized organizations also lose the competition for talent, because the younger generation views centralization as a threat to personal autonomy, choice and happiness and is increasingly sceptical of traditional hierarchies.
subjectOf.abstract: The younger "Millennial" generation view centralization as a threat to personal autonomy, choice, and happiness.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P.M. Vermeulen, Why 'Blockchain' Will Disrupt Corporate Organizations (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3227933

subjectOf.text: At the decentralized stage the individual nodes remain autonomous and the network assigns no fixed roles; coordination comes from alignment on a shared transcendental goal rather than from formal position, so that, as the authors put it, the values are the organization.
subjectOf.abstract: The individual nodes remain autonomous; the network does not have fixed roles for each member. But they are all responding to a higher calling as they unite in purpose.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Introduction to Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782192
scope_conditions: decentralized stage of organization, before a hierarchy has formed

subjectOf.text: Decentralization, though it may look wastefully redundant, gives every member greater autonomous power, whereas centralization limits members' powers and reduces them to cogs in the machine.
subjectOf.abstract: Decentralization, while it may be seen as wastefully redundant, gives every member greater autonomous power. Centralization limits its members' powers, reducing them to mere cogs in the machine.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Introduction to Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782192

subjectOf.text: Because a single global society is emerging in which everyone is densely interconnected, the more efficient and stable arrangement is power decentralization giving individuals and subgroup DAOs autonomous power, not a single power-centralized hierarchy controlling the whole.
subjectOf.abstract: the better, more efficient, more stable state of this global society is an organi- zation that is power decentralized, giving individuals and subgroup DAOs more auton- omous power to contribute to the health and wealth and happiness of all.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of Transcendental Unifying Values for Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782220

subjectOf.text: Individual autonomy and group cohesion reinforce rather than substitute for each other: the network effect is achieved only when individuals subsume their freedom to act in concert with the group, and diminishing one quality diminishes the other.
subjectOf.abstract: The network effect is only achieved when individuals subsume their freedom to act in concert with the group. Again, both individual autonomy and group cohesion need to be balanced to increase both qualities. Diminishing one diminishes the other.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of Transcendental Unifying Values for Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782220

subjectOf.text: The strength of a decentralized organization is measured by summing the power of each member in their individual autonomy, modified by the group's ability to organize and effect its goals in the larger society.
subjectOf.abstract: The strength of a decentralized organization is measured by sum- ming the power of each member in their individual autonomy, but this is modified by the ability of the group to organize and effect its goals in the larger society.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of Transcendental Unifying Values for Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782220

subjectOf.text: Decentralized organizations demand more from their members and return more autonomous power and profit, whereas centralized organizations shelter members in a niche and limit and stultify their power in exchange for security.
subjectOf.abstract: Decentralized organizations demand more from their members and return more, in autonomous power and profit. Centralized organizations shelter their members within a niche in a hierarchy. Centralized organizations limit the power of their mem- bers, stultifying them,
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, The Importance of Transcendental Unifying Values for Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782220

subjectOf.text: Regulatory solutions tracked the characteristics of issuers, so the more decentralized, censorship resistant and autonomous products that regulators could not control were left in a regulatory vacuum that limited their expansion, reach and evolution.
subjectOf.abstract: As a result, the more decentralized products that were more censorship resistant, autonomous, and could not be controlled by regulatory agencies, were largely left in a regulatory vacuum that limited their expansion, reach, and evolution.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization Neutralizers (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808873
scope_conditions: jurisdiction specific regulatory frameworks of the early 2020s

subjectOf.text: Modern philanthropy limits the autonomy of grassroots charitable organizations and substitutes a leveraged and exploitive relationship in which the goals of the donor are served above all.
subjectOf.abstract: there is a growing concern amongst commentators that modern philanthropy limits the autonomy of grassroots charitable organizations and replaces it with a leveraged and exploitive relationship where the goals of the donor are served above all.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How Decentralized Autonomous Organizations Optimize Charitable Giving (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3981021
scope_conditions: grassroots charitable organizations receiving major private philanthropic funding

subjectOf.text: Flatter markets with more diverse interests and talents are more effective and efficient at truth discovery, including price discovery and the identification of ideal solutions to new problems, and decentralization promotes that diversity by improving member autonomy and freedom.
subjectOf.abstract: Flatter markets with more diverse interests and talents are more effective and efficient at achieving truth discovery, like price discovery and the identification of ideal solutions to arbitrary new problems that arise.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, DAO Fallacies (2022). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4067783

subjectOf.text: There is no consistent standard for DAO governance, which pushes each DAO to invent its own structure, and because decentralized governance is complex many of those structures fail to become truly decentralized, autonomous, or organized.
subjectOf.abstract: There is no consistent standard for DAO governance. This leads many DAOs to develop their own governance structure. However, because of the complex nature of decentralized governance, many DAO governance structures fail to become truly decentralized, autonomous, or organized.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Josh Bykowski, Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAO) – A Market Meta Analysis (2023). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4529715

subjectOf.text: AI agents are autonomous software entities that execute specific tasks on behalf of their users, combining computational engineering with cognitive simulation; this stipulated definition anchors the paper's monitoring analysis.
subjectOf.abstract: AI agents are autonomous software entities designed to execute specific tasks on behalf of their users, encompassing a convergence of computational engineering and cognitive simulation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, How can we Best Monitor AI Agents (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5245185

subjectOf.text: Current agent platforms are inadequate on both horns: centralized rating systems defeat the purpose of agent autonomy, while primitive token staking mechanisms produce binary outcomes and fail to capture knowledge graphs.
subjectOf.abstract: Current platforms either use centralized rating systems (defeating the purpose of agent autonomy) or primitive token-staking mechanisms (producing binary outcomes and failing to capture knowledge graphs).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Evolution of Domain-Specific Reputation Systems From Binary Validation to Citation-Weighted Knowledge Attribution (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6192998
scope_conditions: AI agent marketplaces and comparable decentralized collaboration platforms
